hunks.baseline: *That guy was practically tearing up earlier.*
hunks.sol: *The man was even tearing up earlier.*

hunks.baseline: Amnesia—the kind I had only ever seen in dramas. Nothing could have been more convenient in my current situation. I didn’t have to struggle to fit into the game’s setting or even gather information.
hunks.sol: Amnesia—the kind I had only ever seen in dramas. Nothing could have been more convenient in my current situation. I didn’t have to make any effort to fit into the game world or dig up information.

hunks.baseline: All I had to do was lie still, blink at everyone with an expression that said *I don’t know anything*, and let the situation take care of itself. Just like now.
hunks.sol: All I had to do was lie still, blink at everyone with an expression that said *I don’t know anything*, and let events unfold on their own. Just like now.

hunks.baseline: “Do you remember what you just said?”
hunks.sol: “Do you remember what we just went over?”

hunks.baseline: “What did I say?”
hunks.sol: “Which part?”

hunks.baseline: Good grief. He was in his thirties with that face? Apparently, he was still a bachelor too.
hunks.sol: Good grief. He was in his thirties with that face? He wasn’t even married yet.

hunks.baseline: “Correct. And your second brother?”
hunks.sol: “That’s right. And your second brother?”

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung had been mechanically saying, “Correct, correct,” after each answer, but now he tilted his head.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung had been mechanically saying, “That’s right, that’s right,” after each answer, but now he tilted his head.

hunks.baseline: “Oh, my youngest!”
hunks.sol: “Oh no, my youngest!”

hunks.baseline: Leaving the physician’s final words behind, I walked out of Medicine King Hall. A servant with a plain, friendly face was waiting for me at the entrance.
hunks.sol: Leaving the physician’s final words behind, I walked out of Medicine King Hall. A servant with an unassuming, approachable face was waiting for me at the entrance.

hunks.baseline: The servant set off without hesitation. He already seemed to know that I had lost my memory, because whenever we passed a building or a person, he would explain who or what they were in a quiet voice.
hunks.sol: The servant set off without hesitation. He already seemed to know that I had lost my memory, because whenever we passed a building or a person, he would quietly explain who or what they were.

hunks.baseline: Wasn’t this kind of building called a pavilion in China? It had a distinctly old-fashioned charm.
hunks.sol: Wasn’t this the kind of building they called a pavilion in China? It had a distinctly old-fashioned charm.

hunks.baseline: It was unbelievably spacious, too. The moment the servant opened the door, my jaw dropped.
hunks.sol: It was unbelievably spacious too. The moment the servant opened the door, my jaw dropped.

hunks.baseline: There were six rooms on the first floor alone. A sudden wave of curiosity rose in me.
hunks.sol: There were six rooms on the first floor alone. Curiosity suddenly surged through me.

hunks.baseline: The exclamation slipped out the moment the door opened. There were no fluorescent lights, yet the room was bright—thanks to the silk clothes packed onto the shelves along the walls. There was an astonishing amount of them, even at a glance.
hunks.sol: The exclamation slipped out the moment the door opened. There were no fluorescent lights, yet the room was bright—thanks to the silk clothes packed onto the shelves lining the walls. There had to be an incredible number of them.

hunks.baseline: *This bastard has a lot of clothes.*
hunks.sol: *This bastard owns a lot of clothes.*

hunks.baseline: A club rat—no, a pleasure-house regular through and through. I clicked my tongue, closed the door, and went straight to the second room. Then I threw that door open too.
hunks.sol: A club regular—no, a pleasure-house regular through and through. I clicked my tongue, closed the door, and went straight to the second room. Then I threw that door open too.

hunks.baseline: I had underestimated Jin Taekyung. At this point, wasn’t he practically the fashion icon of his era?
hunks.sol: I had underestimated Jin Taekyung. At this point, he might as well have been the fashionista of his age.

hunks.baseline: “…What kind of shopping-addicted bastard is this?”
hunks.sol: “…You fucking shopaholic.”

hunks.baseline: Seriously, what kind of person was he? Seeing three rooms packed completely full of clothes made my throat close up, as if I had swallowed a sweet potato.
hunks.sol: Seriously, what the hell was wrong with this guy? Seeing three whole rooms crammed with clothes left me feeling like I had a sweet potato lodged in my throat.

hunks.baseline: My unease was taking shape, growing heavier by the second. I trudged to the final room. Unlike the others, it clearly hadn’t been used in a long time. I took hold of the rusty handle and slowly pushed.
hunks.sol: My unease was becoming real, growing heavier by the second. I trudged to the final room. Unlike the others, it clearly hadn’t been used in a long time. I took hold of the rusty handle and slowly pushed.

hunks.baseline: Jackpot!
hunks.sol: Yes!

hunks.baseline: The number in parentheses bothered me immensely. I had learned exactly three martial arts so far: the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, the Jin Family’s Spear Technique, and the Jin Family’s Manoeuvre Technique.
hunks.sol: The number in parentheses really bothered me. I had learned exactly three martial arts so far: the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, the Jin Family’s Spear Technique, and the Jin Family’s Manoeuvre Technique.

hunks.baseline: That meant I could learn seven more martial arts. If I filled those slots with nothing but the best techniques, Logout would only be a matter of time.
hunks.sol: That meant I could learn seven more martial arts. If I filled those slots with nothing but worthwhile techniques, Logout would only be a matter of time.

hunks.baseline: Today’s battle against work had been fierce. Jin Wikyung had not left the office once between morning and the present hour, which was approaching midnight. This grueling pace had already continued for two months.
hunks.sol: Today’s battle against work had been fierce. Jin Wikyung had not left the office once since morning, and now it was nearly midnight. This grueling pace had already continued for two months.

hunks.baseline: “You’ve worked hard.”
hunks.sol: “Thank you for your hard work.”

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung rose, stretching his stiff body, and left the office. After all, the owner of that room was not Jin Wikyung, but his father, who had vanished without warning one day.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung hauled his stiff body upright and left the office. After all, the owner of that room was not Jin Wikyung, but his father, who had suddenly vanished one day.

hunks.baseline: His residence was a pavilion in the inner compound at the center of the Jin Family estate, and it took about a quarter hour to walk there.
hunks.sol: His residence was a pavilion in the inner compound at the center of the Jin Family estate, about a quarter hour away on foot.

hunks.baseline: Wipeng, who had followed him like a shadow, draped a thick fur cloak over his shoulders. Jin Wikyung smiled tiredly.
hunks.sol: Wipeng, who followed him like a shadow, draped a thick fur cloak over his shoulders. Jin Wikyung smiled tiredly.

hunks.baseline: “What else can I do? Someone has to play the lady of the house.”
hunks.sol: “What choice do I have? Someone has to play the lady of the house.”

hunks.baseline: “Forget it. The old men are already hounding me enough as it is.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t start. The old men are already hounding me about it.”

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung rubbed his dry eyes. Though he was in his mid-thirties, he remained unmarried. He had kept putting marriage off on the grounds that he was still young, and those delays had added up to more than a decade.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung rubbed his gritty eyes. Though he was in his mid-thirties, he remained unmarried. He had kept putting marriage off on the grounds that he was still young, and those delays had added up to more than a decade.

hunks.baseline: Had he ever been in love? Yes.
hunks.sol: It wasn’t as though he had never been in love.

hunks.baseline: But Jin Wikyung was no immature child. One day, he would become the Family Head and bear responsibility for everyone in the household. If a political marriage could strengthen the family, he considered it a small price to pay.
hunks.sol: But Jin Wikyung was no immature child. One day, he would become the Family Head and bear responsibility for everyone in the household. If a political marriage could strengthen the family, he considered it a small sacrifice to make.

hunks.baseline: “The stars are bright. We almost wouldn’t need torches.”
hunks.sol: “The stars are bright tonight. We almost didn’t need torches.”

hunks.baseline: Sensing the mood, Wipeng changed the subject. Jin Wikyung shook his head. His residence had come into view.
hunks.sol: Sensing his mood, Wipeng changed the subject. Jin Wikyung shook his head. His residence had already come into view.

hunks.baseline: “My lord, why don’t we come back another time? The memory loss is just an excuse. He’s obviously drinking.”
hunks.sol: “My lord, why don’t we come back another time? He’s only using the memory loss as an excuse. He’s obviously in there drinking.”

hunks.baseline: The two men entered the pavilion. The light came from the old room on the far left. Constant creaking sounded from within, as if someone were moving around without pause.
hunks.sol: The two men entered the pavilion. The light came from the old room on the far left. Constant creaking sounded from within, as if someone were moving around nonstop.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung sent the short, heavy reply through Sound Transmission, then moved right up to the door. Through the open crack, he could see what was happening inside.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung sent the short, gruff reply through Sound Transmission, then moved right up to the door. Through the open crack, he could see what was happening inside.

hunks.baseline: Then Wipeng cut in with a wounded expression.
hunks.sol: Wipeng, looking wounded, squeezed in beside him.

hunks.baseline: He rubbed his eyes with his sleeve, but all five senses continued to take in the scene before him exactly as it was.
hunks.sol: He rubbed his eyes with his sleeve, but all five senses kept insisting that the scene before him was real.

hunks.baseline: A sturdy young man muttered continuously as he moved without pause. Countless footprints covered the dusty floor, and more were appearing even now.
hunks.sol: A sturdy young man muttered to himself as he moved without rest. Countless footprints covered the dusty floor, and more were appearing even now.

hunks.baseline: Swish. Stumble.
hunks.sol: Swish. Slip.

hunks.baseline: “Fuck, they made this martial art like shit—aaagh!”
hunks.sol: “Fuck, this martial art is designed like shiiiiit!”

hunks.baseline: It was the Third Young Master. That foul personality and that foul mouth. There was no doubt that he was Jin Taekyung.
hunks.sol: It was the Third Young Master. That god-awful temper and that foul mouth. There was no doubt that he was Jin Taekyung.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung gazed into the room with dazed eyes. Jin Taekyung had fallen over and was hurling vicious curses at the ceiling, but he soon got back up and resumed practicing his footwork.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung gazed into the room with dazed eyes. Jin Taekyung had fallen over and was swearing viciously at the ceiling, but he soon got back up and resumed practicing his footwork.
